thread.title: 'Shark Tank' star Kevin O'Leary: 'Apple is getting cheap again'

author: Scott Gamm
title: 'Shark Tank' star Kevin O'Leary: 'Apple is getting cheap again'
text:
There may be a buying opportunity coming in Apple's ( AAPL ) stock, according to "Shark Tank" star Kevin O'Leary, chairman of O'Shares ETF Investments .
"Apple is getting cheap again. The company makes a lot of money — it's just where will the growth engine be?" he said. "If Apple goes down into the low $140s or into $130s, that's when I'll be re-establishing my position again and it's not far to get there."
On Dec. 24, 2018, amid a broader stock market selloff, Apple shares closed just above $146. On January 3, when the market reacted to downbeat Apple revenue guidance on weaker-than-expected iPhone sales in China , the stock closed above $142 a share.
However, heading into Tuesday's earnings release , Apple is trading at $156.30, a 9.9% gain from Jan 3.
Television personality and businessman Kevin O'Leary takes part in a panel discussion of ABC's reality series "Shark Tank" during the 2013 Winter Press Tour for the Television Critics Association in Pasadena, California, January 10, 2013. REUTERS/Gus Ruelas (UNITED STATES - Tags: ENTERTAINMENT BUSINESS) 更多 O'Leary sold his stake in Apple after the company announced in early November 2018 that it would stop reporting iPhone unit sales. Since then, the stock is down roughly $52 a share.
"I had a gut reaction to that [Apple] call when I was told I would never get unit sales again because to me that is the mother's milk of determining Apple's performance and future. The more phones you sell, the more services you're going to get."
Services refers to the revenue from Apple's app and music store, among other sources.
O'Leary also views Apple as a bellwether for the semiconductor and consumer spaces.
"If [Apple] catches a cold, no one else is immune," he added.
—
